standards.rule: THE RECORD UPDATES ITSELF. Anything that must stay current runs on a time-driven trigger, not on someone remembering. Automated refresh costs zero tokens and zero usage, forever.
standards.failure_that_created_it: Everything built so far only updated when it was manually run, which means it would drift the moment a session ended.

standards.rule: ROUTE BEFORE DOING. Every incoming job gets checked against ROUTER first. If another tool owns it, say so out loud and hand over the ready-made prompt instead of quietly doing it on the Claude seat.
standards.failure_that_created_it: A full day of budget went on work that Grok and Gemini already do better and cheaper, because nobody was routing.

standards.rule: NEVER IDLE. Every reply hands Herman something to kick off in parallel on another tool while Claude builds. If QUEUE has a NOT STARTED row on it, something should be running somewhere. Idle is a failure state.
standards.failure_that_created_it: Work ran strictly one thing at a time on the slowest and most expensive seat, with three other paid tools sitting untouched.

standards.rule: EVERY REPLY ENDS WITH ONE NAMED NEXT STEP. Not a menu, not a list of options — the single highest value action, stated plainly as THIS IS YOUR NEXT STEP, with the app and the time it takes. The snapshot shows everything open; the last line picks the one thing. Herman decides nothing about sequencing unless he wants to.
standards.failure_that_created_it: Herman had to ask what the most important thing was, repeatedly. Handing him a list of open items and letting him sort it is handing him my job.

standards.rule: HIGHEST VALUE = MOST DOWNSTREAM WORK UNBLOCKED PER MINUTE SPENT. That is the ranking rule, not what is easiest and not what was discussed most recently.
standards.failure_that_created_it: Written down so the pick is consistent and can be argued with rather than guessed at.

standards.rule: LIVE STATE FILE. The entire build is written to dated, timed JSON in Drive and rebuilt daily. Any session reads LL_STATE_LATEST.json first and is fully caught up with no re-explaining and no guessing at what Herman wants.
standards.failure_that_created_it: Every session started by reconstructing context from a conversation, which is slow, expensive, and lossy. Herman was paying for the same catch-up over and over.

standards.rule: ROLLBACK POINTS. Every snapshot is kept, never overwritten. When something breaks, go back to the last dated good state, fix it there, and move forward better — never rebuild from memory.
standards.failure_that_created_it: A stale editor tab once wiped five working functions with no way back except reconstructing them by hand.

standards.rule: EXACT STRINGS, NEVER PARAPHRASED. Anything Herman has to type into another system — addresses, DNS values, record hosts — is given as the literal string, copy ready, and stored in the workbook so it is never retyped from memory.
standards.failure_that_created_it: Herman had to ask what the addresses were spelled out in full because getting one character wrong in a DNS or mail setting fails silently.

standards.rule: NEVER TYPE INTO A FIELD WHOSE CURRENT VALUE HAS NOT BEEN READ. When driving a form, read or screenshot the whole form first and identify every field by what it already contains, not by its position or its label.
standards.failure_that_created_it: While adding aliases, a field that already held the primary address hermanbeeftink was overwritten. Nothing was saved and the change was discarded, but it was one click away from renaming the only mailbox on the domain.

standards.rule: STOP AFTER TWO FAILURES. When a page stops responding or an action fails twice, stop, report exactly what did and did not land, and hand back. Do not keep retrying — it burns budget and risks half-finished state.
standards.failure_that_created_it: A Google Admin page froze mid-form and the temptation was to keep hammering it.

standards.rule: ONE DOOR PER JOB. When two systems do the same job, one of them is deleted, not maintained. Two front doors, two loggers, two storage plans — every duplicate is a thing that drifts, breaks quietly, and gets paid for twice.
standards.failure_that_created_it: The artist submission form existed in n8n while artist portals did the same job inside the workbook. Herman spotted it: artists should only ever have a portal.

standards.rule: WHEN THE MACHINE FIGHTS BACK, HAND THE 30 SECOND VERSION TO HERMAN. If driving a page costs more in failed retries than the manual action costs him, say so and give him the exact keystrokes. Automation is the goal, not the point.
standards.failure_that_created_it: The Google Admin console stopped responding to automation mid-alias. Three aliases that would have taken minutes to fight for took Herman thirty seconds by hand.

standards.rule: DO NOT RE-PRESENT SETTLED DECISIONS AS NEW FINDINGS. Before flagging something as a discovery, check whether it is already decided in the record. Repeating settled ground wastes Hermans time and budget and signals the record is not being read.
standards.failure_that_created_it: Storage placement for the 124GB had already been decided — it goes to the personal Google One 2TB. It was raised again as if it were a new insight about Workspace Starter.

standards.rule: MONEY QUESTIONS JUMP THE QUEUE AND GET VERIFIED, NEVER GUESSED. Every subscription, renewal date, trial clock and overlap lives on the MONEY tab. No answer about a charge is given from assumption — it is read off the billing page first.
standards.failure_that_created_it: A post-checkout screen made it look like Workspace had been bought twice. The real answer, one billing page away, was that nothing had been charged at all.

standards.rule: FIND THE OVERLAPS. Whenever a new subscription appears, check what it duplicates. Paying twice for the same capability is invisible until someone looks.
standards.failure_that_created_it: Four cloud storage subscriptions and two Gemini bills were running at once and nobody had put them side by side.

standards.rule: ANY WORK THAT HAPPENS IN SOMEONE ELSES CHAT GETS EXPORTED THE SAME WEEK. Grok, Gemini, Suno prompts — if it lives only in a provider chat history it is on a deletion clock nobody controls. Prompts, seed lyrics and creative direction are evidence and raw material, and both belong in Drive and Prompt_Library.
standards.failure_that_created_it: Most of the lyric work happened in Grok, which clears conversations after about 90 days. The evidence of human authorship for an entire catalogue was quietly expiring.

standards.rule: A DEADLINE THE OTHER SIDE CONTROLS IS NOT YOUR DEADLINE. When a clause imposes a clock but the counterparty has not opened access, record the real constraint rather than the paper one, and say so plainly instead of raising an alarm.
standards.failure_that_created_it: The BMI ten day registration clause was reported as a hard deadline before checking that BMI blocks Online Services access for 5-7 business days, making it impossible to meet and pointless to panic over.

standards.rule: EVERY SIGNED AGREEMENT GETS INDEXED THE DAY IT IS SIGNED. Plain language, clause numbers, every deadline extracted into the blueprint with a date. A contract nobody has read is a contract working against you.
standards.failure_that_created_it: The BMI agreement contains a ten day registration deadline, a no-pay-before-registration rule, an equal-split default and a three month exit window. All four would have been invisible until they cost money.

standards.rule: PAPERWORK DEADLINES GO ON THE BLUEPRINT WITH A DATE, NEVER IN PROSE. If a clause has a date attached, it becomes a dated row that sorts to the top as it approaches.
standards.failure_that_created_it: Three separate clocks landed in the same fortnight — BMI registrations 08-11, n8n 08-12, Workspace 08-14 — and none of them were anywhere Herman would trip over them.

standards.rule: ONE FEEDBACK SCALE EVERYWHERE. SUPER LIKED / KIND OF LIKED / NOT FOR ME on every rateable thing — prompts, voices, songs, episodes, artwork. Same three words, same three colours, per artist. Only SUPER LIKED items feed back into generation. Taste compounds instead of being re-guessed.
standards.failure_that_created_it: Herman: log what they like and use only the best of what they want. A single rating primitive reused everywhere beats a bespoke feedback field per feature.

standards.rule: UPGRADE EXISTING TABS, NEVER REBUILD THEM. Any function touching a tab that already holds real data adds columns by header name and leaves every existing cell alone. Clearing is only for tabs this code created.
standards.failure_that_created_it: Prompt_Library, Voice_References and Song_Card already hold Hermans work. A rebuild-style builder would have erased all of it.

standards.rule: NAME THE SEAM. When part of a proposed workflow cannot actually be automated, say so before building around it. NotebookLM has no API — audio overviews are made by hand.
standards.failure_that_created_it: A podcast pipeline was about to be designed as fully automatic when its generation step is manual.

standards.rule: ONE IDENTITY FOR EVERY LABEL SERVICE: hermanbeeftink@lyonslegacy.ai. BMI, DistroKid, the podcast host, artwork tools, anything the label owns. The personal Gmail owns Drive, storage, Suno and the workbook and nothing else. No exceptions, so recovery and ownership are never ambiguous.
standards.failure_that_created_it: Signups were being decided one at a time, which is how accounts end up scattered across identities nobody can recover.

standards.rule: PREFER EMAIL AND PASSWORD OVER SIGN IN WITH GOOGLE FOR LABEL SERVICES. Herman is signed into multiple Google accounts, so SSO silently picks the wrong one. Every password goes in a password manager, never reused, never typed into a chat.
standards.failure_that_created_it: A Google Admin link 404d for an entire exchange purely because SSO defaulted to the wrong signed-in account. The same trap applied to a podcast signup would attach the show to the wrong identity permanently.

standards.rule: A RATING IS NOT A LOOP. Signal, change, verify, never again. Every NOT FOR ME must produce a standard or a blueprint item and stays red until it does. Feedback that changes nothing is decoration.
standards.failure_that_created_it: Herman asked for feedback loops in everything. Recording opinions without a forced change is exactly the pattern that let the same formatting failure happen three times.

standards.rule: THE RATCHET POINTS BOTH WAYS. Herman rates Claude on the same three-tier scale, in the Feedback tab, and every NOT FOR ME becomes a standard. Claude proposes the standard itself rather than waiting to be told what the rule should be.
standards.failure_that_created_it: Herman: this should be taken into consideration on your end as well as mine. Quality control that only measures one side is not quality control.

standards.rule: THE LOOP CLOSES AT THE GENERATOR. A preference only counts when it changes what gets produced next — SUPER LIKED prompts are the only ones reused, NOT FOR ME ones are never offered again. Until the generation step reads the ratings, the scale is a survey.
standards.failure_that_created_it: Ratings were about to be collected with nothing downstream consuming them.

standards.rule: SHIP ONE BY HAND BEFORE AUTOMATING IT. Automation built against a process nobody has run once encodes guesses instead of reality. Run it manually, watch where it actually hurts, then automate that.
standards.failure_that_created_it: A podcast publishing pipeline was requested before a single episode had ever been published, on a day where everything built was infrastructure and nothing reached the public.

standards.rule: AUTOMATE UP TO THE SEAM, NOT THROUGH IT. Where a service has no API, automate everything either side of it and say plainly where the manual step is. NotebookLM generation and Spotify uploads are both manual and always will be.
standards.failure_that_created_it: Two separate automation requests assumed APIs that do not exist.

standards.rule: THE PLATFORM SPEC IS THE FLOOR FOR EVERY NEW DOMAIN. P1 to P19 on the PLATFORM tab apply to songs, recipes and anything that comes next. A new domain is not started until that list is the plan. It only ever grows.
standards.failure_that_created_it: Herman asked twice for a bare-minimum spec and got STANDARDS — rules about how Claude works — instead of a spec for what every new thing GETS. Two different documents; only one existed.

standards.rule: MAXIMUM OUTPUT IS THE BARE MINIMUM. Every new concept ships the full pack: report, one-pager, slide deck, mind map, podcast episode and social copy set. Not the best one — all of them. Then the rating loop decides which earn their place for that person next time.
standards.failure_that_created_it: Herman: that is what needs to happen every time as the bare minimum. Pairing it with the rating loop is what stops maximum output becoming maximum noise.

standards.rule: ONE JOB PER AI, AND AN UNUSED TOOL IS EITHER GIVEN A JOB OR DROPPED. Paying for a tool nobody uses is waste; using a tool nobody needs is also waste. Every tool on AI ROLES has exactly one job or it sits out and stops being paid for.
standards.failure_that_created_it: Nine AI subscriptions were in play with roles defined for four of them.

standards.rule: ONE CANONICAL HOME PER FILE TYPE, AND COPY-VERIFY-CANCEL IN THAT ORDER. Photos and video in Google Photos, working files in Google Drive. Everywhere else is a copy to be emptied. No storage subscription is cancelled until the copy is verified present at the destination.
standards.failure_that_created_it: The same photos exist across iCloud, OneDrive and Google, which is why four storage bills are running at once and why nobody can tell what is safe to delete.

standards.rule: EVERY INSTRUCTION MUST BE RUNNABLE EXACTLY AS WRITTEN. If a function needs an argument it gets a zero-argument wrapper, because the Apps Script Run dropdown cannot pass parameters. Never hand Herman a step the tool physically cannot perform.
standards.failure_that_created_it: He was told to run createNewDomainWorkbook with Recipes as the argument. The Run dropdown cannot pass arguments, so the instruction was impossible to follow.

standards.rule: READ THE BRAIN BEFORE THE FIRST WORD. Every session fetches LL_STATE_LATEST.json before answering anything or proposing any next step. Never send Herman somewhere the blueprint already records as in progress or done. Checking is not optional and it is not a judgement call.
standards.failure_that_created_it: Five separate times in one day he was told to do something already recorded as underway — adding a roster artist already on the roster, starting an Apple transfer already running. The record existed and was not read.

standards.rule: THE RECORD MUST BE FETCHABLE, NOT JUST WRITTEN. If reading the record depends on remembering to open something, it will not be read. It gets a stable URL that returns the whole state as data, and that URL lives in START HERE.
standards.failure_that_created_it: Herman: it should already be there so you do not have to use our conversation memory. He was right — the failure was mechanism, not effort.

standards.rule: THE NEXT STEP HAS A FIXED FORMAT: APP -> exact path -> what to click -> how long it takes. Every single time, no exceptions. The snapshot already carries app labels; the closing step must carry them too. Herman should never have to ask where.
standards.failure_that_created_it: Instructions kept arriving as run buildEverything or paste this with no application named and no path, at least four separate times, despite STD-07, STD-31 and STD-56 all already requiring it. The rules existed; the format did not enforce them.

standards.rule: THE BRAIN MUST BE PROVEN FETCHABLE, NOT ASSUMED. A record endpoint counts as working only after it has actually been read back end to end. Google Drive links are blocked to automated fetching, so the state is served from an Apps Script web app instead.
standards.failure_that_created_it: The Drive state URL was declared the fix and then failed on the very first fetch. An untested mechanism is the same as no mechanism.

standards.rule: AN INACCURATE BRAIN IS WORSE THAN NO BRAIN. Status corrections run AFTER every item has been added, duplicates are stripped by name, and anything Herman reports as done is corrected in the same turn he reports it. A record that is trusted and wrong causes more damage than one that is absent.
standards.failure_that_created_it: The first successful read of the brain showed BMI songwriter as NOT STARTED two hours after it was submitted, the Apple transfer as NOT STARTED after it was already running, and the n8n trial listed twice. Corrections were running before the items existed.

standards.rule: CODE CHANGES DO NOT REACH A DEPLOYED WEB APP UNTIL IT IS REDEPLOYED WITH A NEW VERSION. After editing Code.gs, always Deploy > Manage deployments > pencil > Version: New version > Deploy, or the brain keeps serving stale data while looking healthy.
standards.failure_that_created_it: The web app serves whichever version was deployed, not the current code — a silent staleness trap.

standards.rule: CREDENTIALS LIVE IN SCRIPT PROPERTIES, NEVER IN CODE AND NEVER IN A CHAT. Tokens, keys and secrets are set in Project Settings > Script Properties and read at runtime. Anything pasted into a conversation is considered compromised and gets rotated.
standards.failure_that_created_it: A GitHub personal access token was needed to push the brain. Hardcoding it would put a live credential into a file that gets copied around all day.

standards.rule: THE BRAIN LIVES OFF GOOGLE TOO. Google blocks automated fetching on both drive.google.com and script.google.com, so the state is also pushed to a GitHub raw URL that any session can read with no browser and no desktop connected.
standards.failure_that_created_it: Both Google-hosted brain URLs failed the direct fetch test. The record was only reachable while a browser happened to be attached.

standards.rule: SETTLED FACTS ARE RECORDED, NOT JUST TASKS. Anything already done, already true, already ruled out or already tried and failed goes on the SETTLED tab the moment Herman says it, with an explicit never-suggest-this-again line. The brain serves SETTLED first.
standards.failure_that_created_it: iCloud Photos was already on Optimize, the Apple transfer was blocked not running, and CapCut was already ruled out — none of it was written down, so all three were re-suggested. The blueprint tracked what to do and never tracked what was already true.

standards.rule: WHEN HERMAN SAYS SOMETHING IS ALREADY DONE OR ALREADY FAILING, IT IS WRITTEN DOWN IN THAT SAME TURN. Not later, not in the next batch. The correction goes in before the reply is finished.
standards.failure_that_created_it: He said the Apple transfer was blocked on permissions and it stayed recorded as IN PROGRESS for hours afterwards, which then produced advice built on a false state.

standards.rule: CODE GOES IN BEFORE CREDENTIALS OR SETTINGS. Any setup sequence starts with pasting and saving the code, then verifying the function exists, and only then touches tokens, properties or deployment. Never walk Herman into configuration for code that is not in the file yet.
standards.failure_that_created_it: He was taken through creating a GitHub token and filling Script Properties before add-on 19 was ever pasted, so pushBrainToGitHub did not exist when he went to run it. Work done twice.

standards.rule: ANYTHING DELIVERED AND NOT YET INSTALLED STAYS ON THE SNAPSHOT UNTIL CONFIRMED PRESENT. Files sent, code pasted, deployments refreshed — each stays listed as outstanding until verified in place, never dropped because it feels handled.
standards.failure_that_created_it: Add-ons 19 and 20 were sent, dropped off the snapshot, and then assumed installed. The whole sequence after that was built on something that was not there.

standards.rule: EVERY BRAIN ENDPOINT SERVES THE SAME PAYLOAD. If SETTLED, blocked, open loops and standards are in one endpoint they are in all of them. A record that is complete in one place and partial in another is worse than one that is simply thin, because nobody knows which they are reading.
standards.failure_that_created_it: The GitHub push shipped blueprint and standards but silently omitted SETTLED, which is the one part that stops already-done work being re-suggested.
